questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that SLA configuration mistakes carry outsized risk compared to ordinary data-entry mistakes?
options: A flawed account rule can silently misstate every transaction of a given type across every ledger it serves, not just one record
Configuration mistakes and data-entry mistakes carry exactly the same risk
Configuration can never actually contain mistakes
Data-entry mistakes are always more costly than configuration mistakes
questions.explain: A single flawed rule has a much larger blast radius than a single data error, since it can affect every matching transaction until corrected.

questions.q: What do data access sets control in Oracle Fusion?
options: Which font is used on the login screen
Which journal line types are seeded by Oracle
The exchange rate used for currency conversion
Which ledgers a given user can see or act on, rather than granting blanket access to every ledger
questions.explain: Data access sets scope a user's visibility and transaction rights to specific ledgers or ledger sets.

questions.q: Why do data access sets matter particularly in multi-ledger, multiple-representation scenarios (from lesson 26)?
options: They don't matter in that scenario at all
Multiple ledgers automatically share identical access for every user
Data access sets only apply to a single-ledger environment
A user might legitimately need access to a primary ledger but have no business reason to touch a secondary ledger built for a different reporting purpose
questions.explain: In multi-ledger setups, a user's legitimate need for one ledger does not imply a need for access to every other ledger, including secondary ones.

questions.q: What is the purpose of segregating who configures Subledger Accounting rules from who processes day-to-day transactions?
options: To slow down transaction processing on purpose
To prevent the same people who enter transactions from also being able to change how those transactions get accounted, providing a check against error and fraud
Because only Oracle Support is allowed to process transactions
Segregation of duties has no real purpose in Subledger Accounting
questions.explain: Separating configuration access from transactional access prevents the same individuals from both entering transactions and controlling how they are accounted.

questions.q: What is the key difference in impact between processing one transaction and configuring one rule?
options: There is no difference; both have identical impact
Configuring a rule only ever affects test environments
Processing a transaction always affects more records than configuring a rule
Processing a transaction affects only that transaction, while configuring a rule affects every future transaction the rule applies to, across every period until changed
questions.explain: A rule change has an ongoing, broad effect on every matching future transaction, unlike a single transaction's isolated impact.
